To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
trkB mRNA is increased bilaterally in dentate gyrus 3-6 h after moderate severity lateral fluid-percusion injury.
trkB mRNA is increased in the dentate granule cell layer following traumatic brain injury.
expression of m-RNA for the neurotrophic factor receptor trkB is increased in the dentate of the hippocampus following a moderate lateral fluid percussion injury.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that regulate neuronal plasticity in the hippocampus.
the molecular and cellular basis of the neuroprotective effects of BDNF in the injured brain and how BDNF may contribute to the pathogenesis of secondary injury processes.
the molecular mechanisms that mediate the effects of traumatic brain injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of trkB is upregulated in dentate gyrus after moderate fluid percussion brain injury.
the expression of trkB and trkC mRNAs are altered in different brain regions following traumatic brain injury.
the expression of trkB and trkC mRNA is altered in the hippocampal dentate gyrus after lateral fluid-percusion brain trauma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of trkB is altered in the hippocampal dentate gyrus after traumatic brain injury and this may be related to BDNF signalling mechanisms.
BDNF and its receptors may have a role in secondary injury mechanisms following traumatic brain injury.

the neurotrophic factors BDNF and NT-3 may be involved in the secondary injury cascade following traumatic brain injury and that the neurotrophin receptors trkB and trkC are differentially modulated in the hippocampus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neurotrophin BDNF and the neurotrophine BDNF receptor TrkB are both upregulated in the brain after traumatic brain injury.
BDNF mRNA expression is increased after TBI, and this is associated with increased trkB mRNA expression in the dentate granule cells, the primary target of BDNF in the brain.
trkB mRNA levels are increased in the rat dentate gyrus after moderate lateral fluid-percusion injury.
